title: Investigation of the Microstructural and Magnetic Properties of Ni on GeSn Layers
authors: Tharundev V, Dushyant Singh, Subha Maity, Vigneshwari S R, Dhammapriy Gayakwad, Shivesh Yadav, Krista R Khiangte
abstract: Thermal processing of nickel (Ni) layers on germanium-tin (GeSn) can strongly modify the Ni film and the Ni/GeSn interface within a restricted thermal budget; however, the influence of GeSn crystalline quality on Ni-Ge-Sn interfacial evolution and the magnetic response of the Ni layer remains incompletely understood. Here, Ni (15~nm)/Ge$_{1-x}$Sn$_x$/Ge/Gd$_2$O$_3$/Si(111) heterostructures ($x = 0.08$ and $0.10$) were investigated following rapid thermal annealing at 573 and 973~K for 10~s using X-ray diffraction, pole-figure analysis, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy depth profiling, and temperature- and field-dependent magnetization measurements. Annealing at 573~K preserves the crystallographic texture of Ge$_{0.92}$Sn$_{0.08}$, whereas Ge$_{0.90}$Sn$_{0.10}$ exhibits microtwin formation and reduced structural integrity. Annealing at 973~K, employed as a severe upper-bound thermal reference, causes extensive structural degradation in both heterostructures, with substantially greater deterioration in the higher-Sn sample. XPS depth profiling reveals progressive Ni-Ge-Sn intermixing accompanied by pronounced Sn surface segregation with increasing annealing temperature. Magnetization measurements show coexisting ferromagnetic and superparamagnetic contributions in the as-deposited and 573~K samples, whereas annealing at 973~K strongly suppresses the ferromagnetic response, producing highly unsaturated $M(H)$ loops together with reduced saturation magnetization and coercivity. These magnetic changes are consistent with extensive interfacial alloying and dilution of the metallic Ni layer. This study establishes a direct correlation between GeSn crystalline quality, interfacial diffusion, and magnetic behavior.
summary: This work investigates how thermal annealing affects the magnetic properties of Ni layers deposited on GeSn semiconductor heterostructures. By combining structural, chemical, and magnetic characterization, the authors establish a direct link: poor GeSn crystalline quality or high annealing temperatures lead to severe interfacial diffusion and structural degradation, which in turn suppresses the intrinsic ferromagnetic magnetism of the Ni film.
main_problem: The study investigates how the crystalline quality of GeSn layers influences the interfacial evolution between Ni and GeSn, and how this, in turn, affects the magnetic properties of the Ni film under thermal processing.
main_result: The magnetic response is strongly correlated with the structural integrity of the GeSn layer; high annealing temperatures cause significant interfacial alloying and structural degradation, leading to a suppression of the ferromagnetic signal.
method: The researchers used a combination of structural characterization (XRD, pole-figure analysis), chemical analysis (XPS depth profiling), and magnetic measurements (M(H) and M(T)) on layered heterostructures.
model_or_system: The physical system is a $	ext{Ni} / 	ext{Ge}_{1-x}	ext{Sn}_x / 	ext{Ge} / 	ext{Gd}_2	ext{O}_3 / 	ext{Si}(111)$ heterostructure, where $x$ is the Sn concentration (0.08 or 0.10). These stacks are subjected to rapid thermal annealing (RTA) at temperatures like 573 K and 973 K.
key_observables: Microstructure (crystallographic texture, microtwin formation), Interfacial composition (Ni-Ge-Sn intermixing, Sn segregation), and Magnetic properties (Ferromagnetic saturation magnetization ($M_{FM}^S$), coercivity ($H_c$), and the transition between ferromagnetic and superparamagnetic states).
important_parameters: Sn concentration ($x=0.08, 0.10$), Annealing temperatures (573 K, 973 K), and the time duration (10 s).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that changes in magnetic behavior are directly traceable to changes in interfacial alloying and the resulting dilution of the metallic Ni layer.
figures_summary: XRD scans show peak shifts and loss of fringes indicating lattice changes. Pole figures confirm structural degradation, with $	ext{Ge}_{0.90}	ext{Sn}_{0.10}$ showing microtwins at 573 K and complete pole loss at 973 K. Magnetization loops show a clear suppression of the ferromagnetic signal at 973 K.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes structural changes (XRD/Pole Figure) to establish the degree of crystalline degradation, followed by chemical analysis (XPS) to quantify intermixing, and finally correlates these findings with magnetic measurements ($M(H)$) to draw conclusions about the physical mechanisms governing magnetic loss.
why_interesting: While the focus is materials science, the study involves the interplay between structural disorder (crystallinity, alloying) and emergent magnetic properties, which touches upon concepts relevant to disordered magnetic systems studied in condensed matter theory.

figures.caption: Figure 1. θ-2θ scans of Ni/Ge(1−x)Snx/Ge//Gd2O3 Si(111) samples: (a-c) x = 8% for RTA at 973 K, RTA at 573 K, and as-deposited conditions; (d-f) x = 10% for RTA at 973 K, RTA at 573 K, and as-deposited conditions.

Figure 2. XRD pole figure measurements were carried out at the Bragg angle corresponding to the GeSn(111) reflection. Figures (a)-(c) present the pole figure measurements for Ge0.92Sn0.08 in the as-deposited state and after RTA at 573 K and 973 K, respectively. Figures (d)-(f) show the corresponding measurements for Ge0.90Sn0.10 under the same conditions.

Figure 3. XPS depth profile spectra of the as-deposited Ni/Ge1−xSnx/Ge/Gd2O3/Si(111) layered structure for two Sn concentrations. Panels (a), (b), and (c) show the Ni 2p3/2, Ge 2p3/2 and Sn 3d spectra for Ge0.92Sn0.08 sample respectively. Similarly, panel (d), (e) and (f) show the Ni 2p3/2, Ge 2p3/2 and Sn 3d spectra for Ge0.90Sn0.10 sample respectively. Each spectrum represents successive sputtering cycles (0 to 11 cycle) from the surface into the film, illustrating the evolution of chemical states across the Ni/GeSn interface.
